**Stacked on `master`.** The service half of the old #927; 🟣 #927 is now the screen alone. ## One record A `Claim` with a `status`: **submitted → approved | declined**. `ClaimSubmission` and `DeclinedFigure` are gone — the first was a Claim wearing another name (same shape, context, citation) and the second was a third record saying a claim was never made. Every field but `status` is `Field(frozen=True)`, and `save` refuses a fresh record written over a stored id. So the value a reader saw still cannot change, and the lifecycle can. ```mermaid flowchart LR F["a figure whose rule
names a claim shape"] -->|submit + context| S["Claim
submitted"] F -->|skip| D["Claim
declined"] S -->|approve, re-checked| A["Claim
approved"] S -->|reject| D D -->|submit after all| S ``` **A declined claim stays, saying so.** That is what tells a figure looked at and refused from one nobody opened — which is what makes the run's tally honest, and next run it is the thing you most want to see. Only claims that stand or await review are offered as another claim's history. **Approval re-checks.** What was in the way can move while a claim waits — another claim reaching `approved` for the same context — and a check made only at submission would let that through. ## Context, typed A shape declares its axes; a claim supplies a member for each. Time is one of them and nothing else is special about it. A member is `period` (two dates), `point` (an instant) or `term` (a word), so two claims are one fact when the **dates** match rather than when the spellings do — and the questions a series needs later stay askable: overlaps, contains, adjacent. Which makes the guarantee expressible: **one shape and one context is one fact**, so a second value for it is a restatement and submit refuses it. A different member is a series and goes through. ## Not here No workflow version: #974 took it off `Claim` and nothing else has a claim to it — the citation names a run and the run names its version. No withdrawal or supersession: reachable from no button, and retiring a standing claim is a review act. +817, of which 350 is tests. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**Stacked on 🟣 #925 (`feat/mint-claims`).** The service half of the old #927, which is now the screen alone. ## What a run's figure goes through ```mermaid flowchart LR F["a figure whose rule
names a claim shape"] --> S["submit_for_review
+ context"] F --> D["decline_figure
per run, no reason"] S --> A["approve_submission
re-checks, then writes"] S --> R["reject_submission"] A --> C["Claim"] R --> D ``` ## Three decisions worth your eye **Approving is what writes the claim, and it re-checks first.** What stands in the way can move while a submission waits — another run publishing a claim for the same context — so a check made only at submission time would let that through. **One shape and one context is ONE FACT.** A second value for the same context is a restatement and is refused; a different member is a series and goes through. This is the "have I contradicted myself" check, and it could not exist before context did. **A member is typed.** `period` carries two dates, `point` an instant, `term` a word. Two claims are one fact when the dates match rather than when the spellings do — no `Q1-Q2 2026` vs `Q1–Q2 2026` — and it keeps the questions a series needs later askable: overlaps, contains, adjacent. ## Cut from the old #927 Withdrawal and supersession. They were reachable from no button, and retiring a standing claim is a review act — they belong with review, not here. +812, of which 350 is tests. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
